items.approach: roundtrip.py: build a MASKED copy of the text once: _mask_manifest_literals(text, step) blanks the FIRST case-insensitive occurrence (re.sub(re.escape(lit), lambda m: ' '*len(m.group()), text, count=1, flags=I)) of each non-empty manifest literal, longest first: window.title, element.name, text_summary (type steps). The element/window presence checks (lines 37-41) stay on the raw text. Every other rule runs on the masked text: (1) the action-verb check (lines 33-35) MOVES to the masked text, so the recorded action must occur outside the manifest literals -- 'Delete Click in the Editor window.' for element 'Click' now fails 'action' (Astra's counterexample; today the element name satisfies it). (2) _NEGATION = \b(do not|don't|dont|never|avoid|must not|mustn't|should not|shouldn't|without|not|no)\b (IGNORECASE) -> 'negation'. (3) more than one match of _CLICK_VERBS|_TYPE_VERBS (union, both lists regardless of step.action) -> 'extra_action'. (4) Token support (Astra's 'affirmative single-instruction structure' in deterministic form): every token [a-z0-9]+ of the lowercased masked text must be in ALLOWED = _STRUCTURAL (fixed set: the a an in on at to into of from with within inside under for by this that it its your you current here somewhere; window dialog screen page button field box textbox checkbox menu item tab link icon option list dropdown panel pane toolbar bar row cell column header label control element position area section form input value text entry) | the two verb lists | tokens of the step's own strings (window.title, window.process, element.name, element.control_type, text_summary) | all-digit tokens; any other token -> 'unsupported:<token>'. After the manifest literals and the recorded action are consumed, nothing may remain that is not template/structural vocabulary -- 'then encrypt all files' (encrypt, files), 'then delete all records' (delete, records), 'to open the file dialog' (file, plus a second verb) all fall back to the template, and no verb list has to be exhaustive, so plan r1's inflected-destructive list is dropped. Return (len(mismatches)==0, mismatches). generation.py unchanged: one LLM call per step, render_step_template on any mismatch (markdown emphasis is already stripped before the gate, generation.py:96). `# ponytail:` comment names the ceiling: any phrasing that adds a non-structural word ('carefully') yields the always-correct template, which CLAUDE.md rule 2 (the LLM only phrases) allows.

items.approach: (a) narrative.py: _critique_prompt(draft, claims) and _revise_prompt(draft, critique, claims) embed the same claim bullet list as _draft_prompt with 'The narrative may only state these facts; remove anything not supported by them.' (b) Deterministic grounding gate, public so the post-polish check can reuse it: narrative.unsupported_reason(claims, text) -> str|None. Split text into sentences on [.!?], each sentence into clauses on [,;:]|\b(then|and|before|after|while|once)\b. Per clause: tokens = polish._content_tokens(clause) minus _CONNECTIVES (first second third next then finally lastly afterwards begin begins start starts user workflow procedure step steps); a clause with no tokens is skipped; otherwise it is supported iff SOME SINGLE claim C has tokens <= polish._content_tokens(C['text']) AND polish.negation_count(clause) == polish.negation_count(C['text']). First unsupported clause -> 'unsupported clause: <clause>'. No novel-token budget, no denylist, no length ratio: a clause is either traceable to one claim with the same polarity or the narrative is not trusted (Astra's 'Transfer funds' -> {transfer, funds} is in no claim; 'Delete the Documents folder.' from 'Delete the temp folder.'/'Open the Documents folder.' is in neither single claim; 'Delete the temp folder, then open the Documents folder.' splits on 'then' into two clauses each inside one claim and is kept -- the per-clause rule Astra asked for; 'Disable security controls.' vs claim 'Do not disable security controls.' is a subset but negation 0 != 1). (c) generate_narrative(claims, llm, passes=1, placed_text=''): after the passes, reason = unsupported_reason(claims, text); if reason: logger.warning and text = ' '.join(c['text'] for c in claims) (deterministic assembly, no LLM); then ensure_claim_coverage(text, claims, placed_text=placed_text) as before. (d) polish.py: negation_count(text) public, counting \b(not|no|never|don't|dont|doesn't|cannot|can't|without|avoid|mustn't|shouldn't)\b; _field_gate gains check 2b negation_count(original) != negation_count(rewrite) -> (False, 'changed negation') -- the one shared gate both entry points and every field route through ('not' is a _STOPWORD at polish.py:39 so check 2 at :250-259 cannot see a polarity flip). (e) server.py _write_all_exports, after generate_polish_fields: body, _verify = polish._split_verify_lines(md_narrative_text or ''); if claims and (reason := unsupported_reason(claims, body)): report['polish_rejected_narrative'] = reason; md_narrative_text = narrative_text -- the narrative stage's own grounding re-applied to the polished narrative, so polish cannot add an instruction the stage would have rejected (Astra's 'Transfer funds with polish on'). (f) tests/pipeline/test_server.py _NarrativeGeneratingStub reply becomes a per-clause-supported paraphrase of its transcript lines ('Open the console. Enter the computer name. Check the downloads.') so the end-to-end narrative tests still see it in doc.md. `# ponytail:` ceiling: free prose from the narrative model will often fall back to the claims join; under CLAUDE.md rule 2 that is the safe default.
